rationale.conceptual: The paper applies the cluster expansion formalism (Connolly-Williams) to a specific pseudobinary system. This requires understanding formation energy definitions, fitting ECI by linear regression, and computing solubility from free-energy minimization. It is an established but non-trivial method needing careful implementation of a documented multi-part algorithm.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has 4 main stages: structure enumeration, DFT calculations (~230 small unit cells), ECI fitting, and solubility computation. Integrating tools (ATAT, open-source DFT) and orchestrating the batch of DFT runs adds moderate engineering complexity, though each step is straightforward once set up.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires reproducing a cluster expansion thermodynamic analysis of Pd-Ru-Te phases using DFT and fitting ECI, which involves generating ~230 structures, running DFT calculations, fitting coefficients, and deriving solubility limits. The method is non-trivial but uses standard tools (cluster expansions, DFT) and requires careful implementation of the multi-step pipeline, though the actual computation scales modestly.

compute_estimate.reasoning: DFT calculations on unit cells with a few atoms (hcp/fcc ≤ 6 atoms, PdTe ~4 atoms, Pd20Te7 larger) using k-point meshes up to 15x15x15 – total ~230 structures – can be run on CPUs with a few GB RAM; input files and outputs are tiny.
